name: Ireland
tagline: A small wet island that exported its writers, its music and a third of its people, and kept the landscape.
summary: Ireland is green because it rains, and the rain arrives from the Atlantic in bands with sun between them. The west is the draw: limestone pavement, sea cliffs, a language still spoken daily, and traditional music played in pubs for the players rather than the audience. Dublin is small for a capital and dense with literary ghosts.

season.note: May and September give the best odds of dry days and the roads are passable. Summer is busy on the Wild Atlantic Way and accommodation in Kerry books out months ahead. Winter is dark, cheap and atmospheric if you want fires and sessions.

getting_around: Dublin to Galway and Cork by train is easy; everything else really wants a car, and the small roads are small. Buses reach the peninsulas slowly. Ferries serve the Aran Islands from Rossaveel and Doolin.
food: Brown soda bread with butter and smoked salmon
Oysters from Galway Bay, September onwards
Seafood chowder, which is a meal and a test of a pub

festivals.name: Fleadh Cheoil, the traditional music championship

know: Ireland is in the EU but not Schengen; the Common Travel Area with the UK works separately.
Traditional sessions are for the musicians — sit, listen, and do not clap over the tune's end.
Rural addresses often have no street numbers; Eircodes work where satnav does not.

regions.name: Dublin & the East
regions.summary: The capital, its literature, and a monastic valley in the mountains behind it.

cities.name: Dublin
cities.summary: Georgian squares, a 1,200-year-old river crossing, and four Nobel laureates in literature from one small city.
highlights: The Book of Kells and the Long Room at Trinity
Kilmainham Gaol, where the 1916 leaders were executed
The National Gallery and the Hugh Lane, both free
A session in the Cobblestone rather than Temple Bar

experiences.name: A real session, not a show
experiences.summary: Musicians sit in a circle facing each other, not the room; the etiquette is quiet during tunes and buy the round.

places.name: The Long Room, Trinity College
places.summary: Sixty-five metres of oak barrel vault holding 200,000 of the library's oldest books, with the Book of Kells shown below it a page at a time.

places.name: Kilmainham Gaol
places.summary: Where the leaders of the 1916 Rising were held and shot. Guided entry only, and the tours sell out days ahead — which is the single most useful thing to know about visiting Dublin.

cities.name: Glendalough
cities.summary: A 6th-century monastic city in a glacial valley with two lakes, an hour from Dublin.
highlights: The round tower, 30 metres, built as a bell tower and a refuge
The Spinc ridge walk above the upper lake
Early morning, before the coaches from Dublin

places.name: The Round Tower and monastic city
places.summary: A sixth-century monastic settlement in a glacial valley, with a 30 m round tower whose door is four metres off the ground for reasons nobody has to explain twice.

regions.name: The West & the Atlantic
regions.summary: Galway, the Burren's limestone, the Aran Islands and the cliffs.

cities.name: Galway
cities.summary: A small port city that plays music every night of the week and treats a festival as its natural state.
highlights: Music in the Latin Quarter, from about nine
Oysters and Guinness at a bar that shucks them in front of you
The Salthill prom walk, and kicking the wall at the end

experiences.name: Oysters at the counter
experiences.summary: Native flat oysters from the bay outside, September to April; a dozen, brown bread, and no ceremony.

cities.name: The Aran Islands (Inis Mór)
cities.summary: Three limestone islands where Irish is the daily language and stone walls divide fields the size of rooms.
highlights: Dún Aonghasa, a prehistoric fort on an 87-metre cliff with no railing
1,600 km of dry stone wall on an island 14 km long
Bicycles, because there is almost nothing else

experiences.name: The island by bicycle
experiences.summary: Hire at the pier, ride the length of it, and be back for the last ferry — the island's whole scale in one day.

cities.name: Dingle
cities.summary: A fishing town on a peninsula of beehive huts, empty beaches and the westernmost point of Europe's mainland fringe.
highlights: The Slea Head drive, and stopping at the clocháin
Gallarus Oratory, dry-stone and watertight after 1,200 years
Music in pubs that are also hardware shops

places.name: Slea Head
places.summary: The western end of the peninsula, looking at the Blasket Islands, with beehive huts and an oratory built without mortar that has stayed dry for twelve hundred years.
